current_events: The Ras Tanura oil refinery in Saudi Arabia's Eastern Province is damaged in an attack by the Houthis

A Hamas security official, his wife, and two daughters, are killed in an Israeli airstrike on the Al-Shati refugee camp near Gaza City. Seven more Palestinians are also killed and several injured in more Israeli airstrikes
An Islamic State suicide bomber blows himself up on a motorcycle at a checkpoint in Hasakah, Syria, killing two security forces and wounding five more
Aftermath of the Syrian civil war

Bangladesh's Minimum Wage Board raises the monthly minimum wage for garment workers from ৳12,500 to ৳17,000 following a 4–2 vote, a decision rejected by labour unions demanding at least ৳18,000 amid nearly a month of labour unrest and hundreds of factory closures

At least 140 garment factories close across Gazipur, Savar, and Ashulia, after workers reject the newly announced minimum wage as insufficient, blocking the Dhaka–Mymensingh and Dhaka–Tangail highways and clashing with police firing tear gas and stun grenades
2026 Bangladesh garment workers protests

Thousands of workers across Greece stage a strike demanding higher wages, restored public-sector bonuses, and increased funding for education and healthcare, disrupting ferry, metro, and air services. Police report approximately 15,000 demonstrators in Athens

The European Union and United Kingdom impose fines totalling more than €570 million (US$626 million) on fragrance manufacturers Firmenich, Givaudan, and International Flavors & Fragrances for exchanging commercially sensitive information and cartel behavior between 2019 and 2023
Thirty-one people are killed and 25 more injured after the overturn and explosion of a fuel tanker on Ring Road in Cairo, Egypt
2026 Giza fuel tanker explosion
Six people die in the crash of a Cessna 210 Centurion carrying a family from a fishing trip near Horn Island, Mississippi, United States
The United States Army detonates nearly 5 tons of degrading lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown, Iowa, citing spontaneous explosion risks

Solomon Islands prime minister Matthew Wale signs a treaty with Australian prime minister Anthony Albanese to designate Australia as the "primary security partner" after ending the 2022 security pact with China
Australia–Solomon Islands relations

The Cambodian and Chinese militaries begin their largest joint exercise, Golden Dragon 2026, involving nearly 3,000 personnel across three locations in Cambodia, focusing on counterterrorism, anti-piracy operations, and humanitarian assistance

Border Guard Bangladesh deploys 108 platoons across Dhaka and seven other districts, including 56 in Gopalganj, under instructions from the Ministry of Home Affairs to step up surveillance at key installations and industrial zones
Aftermath of the July Uprising, 2026 Bangladesh garment workers protests
Salvadoran national Kilmar Abrego Garcia arrives in Madrid, Spain, after voluntarily leaving the United States following a legal dispute over his wrongful deportation to El Salvador in March 2025
Deportation of Kilmar Abrego Garcia

A federal jury in Brooklyn, New York, United States, finds Huawei and three of its subsidiaries guilty on 10 of 12 counts, including bank fraud, wire fraud, money laundering, conspiracy to steal trade secrets, and violating the International Emergency Economic Powers Act by misleading banks about its business in Iran

The Federal Supreme Court rules that the federal government of Iraq can deploy troops to the country's borders and can oversee and audit the oil industry in the Kurdistan Region, a day after Iraqi prime minister Ali al-Zaidi announced he is placing the region's oilfields and border crossings under federal control to combat oil smuggling

Pakistani astronaut Muhammad Zeeshan Ali becomes the first Pakistani to reach orbit and the first foreign national to board China's Tiangong space station, arriving aboard the Shenzhou-24 spacecraft alongside two Chinese astronauts to conduct scientific experiments during a five-day mission
